name: Conductor

runner.notes: Prepare the benchmark fixture as a Git repository, import it into the macOS app, create one Conductor workspace per run, select the guest agent/model, provide prompt.md, and verify the resulting workspace. Record local versus Cloud execution, Conductor version, guest agent/model, subscription, and every human intervention as separate run dimensions.

inclusion: Direct multi-agent ADE competitor combining parallel agent sessions, Git-worktree isolation, review and pull-request workflow, and optional cloud orchestration.
pricing_model: The local macOS app is described as free in the official FAQ; Conductor Pro gates the Cloud API and early-access multiplayer, while public plan prices were not verified in this review.
public_stack_signals: Proprietary macOS desktop application; Windows and Linux are not available according to the installation docs.
Local workspaces use Git worktrees and one branch per workspace under ~/conductor/workspaces.
Conductor Cloud runs isolated microVM sandboxes with repositories and dependencies pre-installed.
Cloud automation is exposed through a bearer-authenticated HTTP API under https://api.conductor.build/v0.
Repository configuration can be shared through .conductor/settings.toml; machine-local overrides use .conductor/settings.local.toml.
capabilities_to_probe: parallel Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode sessions
one-workspace-per-task Git worktree and branch isolation
multiple agents sharing one workspace and branch
setup/run scripts, copied ignored files, and per-workspace ports
diff comments sent back to agents, agent review, checks, PR creation, merge, archive, and restore
Cloud microVM startup, persistence, API supervision, and recovery
multiplayer shared workspaces and real-time collaborative prompting
background tasks and agent-to-agent orchestration through the Conductor API
moat_hypotheses: polished worktree-first desktop workflow spanning agent execution, live app testing, review, checks, and pull requests
hybrid local and cloud workspace model with the same agent-facing product surface
first-party support for several leading coding-agent CLIs while preserving users' existing subscriptions and keys
programmable cloud fleet API plus multiplayer collaboration can extend the product from individual ADE to team control plane
setup_notes: Local benchmarking currently requires macOS, GitHub CLI authentication, and login for at least one supported agent provider.
Use a separate run for Conductor Cloud because microVM isolation, provisioning, billing, latency, and API supervision are not parity-equivalent to the local worktree mode.
Do not treat Git worktrees as a security boundary: the official docs state that local agents retain the macOS user's filesystem and command permissions.

research.positioning: A macOS and cloud control plane for running teams of first-party coding agents in isolated workspaces, then reviewing, testing, and shipping each branch through an integrated diff, checks, and pull-request workflow.

runtime: First-party Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode processes
Local macOS execution under the user's permissions
Cloud agents in isolated microVM sandboxes
frontend: Cloud workspace surface with real-time multiplayer
Conductor API for custom clients and integrations
backend: Local Git worktree and process orchestration
Cloud workspace/session service exposed through a beta HTTP API
packaging: Cloud service and Pro-gated API/multiplayer features
data: Local workspaces, chats, and repository files remain on the Mac unless sent to a connected provider or integration
Workspace notes and handoffs can live in a gitignored .context directory
Cloud API exposes projects, workspaces, sessions, messages, status, and read-only transcript search
unknowns: Desktop implementation language and UI framework are not published.
Cloud control-plane implementation, microVM provider, tenancy details, retention, and regional availability were not verified.
Public plan prices, quotas, and Cloud compute limits were not verified.

infrastructure: Local mode creates a Git worktree and branch per workspace; setup scripts, run scripts, terminals, app processes, chat, diff, PR state, and archive actions stay attached to that workspace.
Multiple independent tasks run in separate workspaces, while multiple agents can share one workspace when they need the same branch and latest filesystem state.
Cloud mode provisions isolated microVMs from repository snapshots and can be driven from the desktop product, shared workspace links, or the HTTP API.

agent_support: First-party Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode agents.
Uses existing local provider authentication, subscriptions, or API keys in local mode.
orchestration: Parallel agents across independent workspaces and multiple agents sharing one workspace.
Cloud API can create workspaces and sessions, send prompts, read replies, inspect status, cancel turns, archive workspaces, and supervise multi-PR work.
Background tasks and agents inside Cloud workspaces can invoke the workspace-scoped Conductor API.
workspace_isolation: One Git worktree, branch, files, terminal, processes, context, and review path per local workspace.
Cloud workspaces run in isolated microVM sandboxes.
Local worktree separation is development isolation, not a security or authority boundary.
review_shipping: Diff viewer with inline comments, file reverts, agent review, and GitHub review-thread resolution.
Checks surface for Git status, PR metadata, CI, deployments, comments, and todos.
Integrated PR creation, merge, archive, history, and restore workflow.
remote_mobile: Cloud workspaces can be accessed from desktop and shared through workspace links.
Official site advertises mobile and custom API integrations; native iOS is marked as forthcoming.
context_memory: Chat, diff, PR state, terminal state, archive actions, and task context remain attached to the workspace.
Repository guidance can be checked into .conductor/settings.toml; task notes and handoffs can use .context.
integrations: GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests, checks, deployments, and review comments.
MCP servers, custom providers, deep links, and beta HTTP API.

install_surface: Download and install the macOS application from conductor.build.
Authenticate GitHub CLI and at least one supported guest agent.
Import the prepared fixture repository and configure setup/run scripts without changing the benchmark prompt.
For Cloud measurement, provision a Pro account/API key and record Cloud configuration and cost separately.
parity_risks: Single-agent correctness primarily measures the selected guest agent/model; Conductor-specific value needs parallelism, isolation, intervention, review, recovery, and shipping metrics.
Local mode is macOS-only and uses host-user permissions, while Cloud mode changes compute, security boundary, network, provisioning, and billing.
Existing provider subscriptions and keys can produce materially different cost and rate-limit conditions.
Cloud API and multiplayer are beta/early-access surfaces and may change during a benchmark cycle.

hypotheses: A cohesive path from isolated agent workspace through live app testing, review, checks, PR, merge, and archive reduces coordination overhead beyond a terminal multiplexer.
Supporting local worktrees and cloud microVMs under one workspace abstraction can serve both individual developers and collaborative teams.
A programmable fleet API and real-time multiplayer workspace model may compound through internal tooling and team workflows.
Broad first-party agent support lets Conductor benefit from model/runtime competition without owning a coding model.
evidence: Official docs describe the workspace as the durable unit connecting branch, working tree, agent chats, terminals, diff, checks, PR state, and archive/restore lifecycle.
Official API docs expose programmatic workspace/session creation, prompting, transcript reads, status polling, cancellation, archival, and read-only transcript search.
The July 2026 changelog and homepage document Cloud microVMs, multiplayer, API access, background tasks, and agent-driven child workspace creation.
unknowns: Adoption and retention attributable specifically to Cloud, API, or multiplayer are not publicly verified.
Whether the beta orchestration API gains durable task contracts, verification attestations, scoped agent authority, or approval governance is unknown.
Cloud unit economics, reliability, security certifications, and enterprise controls beyond the published privacy setting remain unverified.
